Socio-economic Benefits and Decent Rural Employment25 239. The proposed intervention is designed to deliver significant socio-economic benefits and promote decent rural employment by fostering sustainable livelihoods and enhancing income opportunities for local communities. Through the adoption of integrated land, water, and natural resource management practices, the project will support the development of alternative, nature-based income-generating activities that align with environmental conservation goals. Initiatives such as agroforestry, conservation agriculture, and improved water management strategies will create opportunities for job creation, particularly in rural areas where employment options are often limited. The establishment of Community-Led Councils and Farmer Field Schools will ensure inclusive participation, capacity building, and skill development, empowering women, youth, and marginalized groups to engage in productive and sustainable economic activities. By prioritizing local knowledge, participatory decision-making, and gender inclusivity, the project will contribute to long-term socio-economic resilience and improved quality of life for rural communities. [25] Specific guidance on how FAO can promote the Four Pillars of Decent Work in rural areas is provided in the Quick reference for addressing decent rural employment reference for addressing decent rural employment (as well as in the full corresponding Guidance document). To strengthen and enhance the functions and services of agro-woodlands and forest ecosystems in the Naryn River basin through a holistic, IWM-based approach to restore terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems and enhance rural community resilience.
